'''Andreas Brandstädt''' (born 17 January 1949 in [[Arnstadt]], [[East Germany]]) is a German [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]].

==Life and work==
He graduated from the Friedrich Schiller [[University of Jena]], Germany, with a Ph.D. (Dr. rer. nat.) in stochastics in 1976 and a habilitation (Dr. sc. nat.) in complexity theory in 1983.
Since 1974 he worked there in the group of his academic teacher [[Gerd Wechsung]].

From 1991 to 1994, he was the professor for Computer Science in the Department of Mathematics,
<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.uni-due.de/mathematik/en_index.php | title=Faculty of Mathematics of the University of Duisburg-Essen}}</ref> at the [[University of Duisburg]], Germany,
and from 1994 to 2014 he was the professor for Theoretical Computer Science<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://users.informatik.uni-rostock.de/~ab | title=A. Brandstädt's Home Page}}</ref> at the [[University of Rostock]], Germany.

He was a visiting professor at the universities of [[University of Metz|Metz]], [[University of Amiens|Amiens]], and [[University of Clermont-Ferrand|Clermont-Ferrand]] (France) and at the [[University of Primorska]] in [[Koper]]
([[Slovenia]]). He was Invited Speaker at various conferences in Argentina, Austria, [[Belarus]], Brasil, Canada, China, France, Greece, India, Israel, Norway, Poland, [[Slovenia]], and Switzerland.

Brandstädt is an active researcher in [[graph algorithms]], [[discrete mathematics]], [[combinatorial optimization]], and [[graph theory]]. A frequently used tool in his papers is tree structure of graphs and hypergraphs such as for [[hypertree]]s, [[strongly chordal graph]]s and [[chordal graph]]s.

He frequently took part in program committees such as Workshop on Graph-Theoretic Concepts in Computer Science (and four times was a co-organizer of this
conference) and is member of the [[Editorial Board]] of [[Discrete Applied Mathematics]].<ref>http://www.journals.elsevier.com/discrete-applied-mathematics/editorial-board/ Editorial Board of Discrete Applied Mathematics</ref>

* Andreas Brandstädt,  Van Bang Le, and Jeremy P. Spinrad [http://epubs.siam.org/doi/book/10.1137/1.9780898719796 ''Graph Classes: A Survey'', SIAM Monographs on Discrete Mathematics and Applications, Philadelphia, PA, 1999, 2nd edition 2004] {{ISBN|0-89871-432-X}}
* Andreas Brandstädt, Feodor Dragan, Victor Chepoi, and Vitaly Voloshin, [http://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S0895480193253415 Dually chordal graphs, ''SIAM J. Discrete Math. Vol. 11, No. 3, pp. 437–455,'' 1998]
* Andreas Brandstädt, Feodor Dragan, and Ekkehard Köhler, [http://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S0097539799357775 Linear time algorithms for Hamiltonian problems on (claw,net)-free graphs, ''SIAM J. Comput. Vol 30 No. 5, pp. 1662–1677,'' 2000]
* Andreas Brandstädt, Van Bang Le, and R. Sritharan, [http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?doid=1435375.1435386 Structure and linear-time recognition of 4-leaf powers, ''ACM Transactions on Algorithms Vol. 5, Issue 1, Article No. 11,'' 2008] 
* Andreas Brandstädt and Raffaele Mosca, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00453-012-9709-4 Dominating Induced Matchings for P7-Free Graphs in Linear Time, ''Algorithmica Vol 68, pp. 998–1018,'' 2014]
